closes: Adds jackknife+/CV+ (finite-sample >=1-2alpha coverage guarantee) to the module UQ battery.
Quantifies the data-efficiency gap between held-out-calibration (split) and full-pool (J+/CV+) conformal on OpenPoly Tg.
does_not_close: Does not establish wet-lab qualification, batch release, or human parity.
Coverage is MARGINAL, not conditional (group-conditional/Mondrian coverage remains untested).
Ridge base learner is a deterministic reference, not the module's production predictor.
headline: Jackknife+ and CV+ (Barber et al. 2021) are added to the tolerance-robustness UQ battery: on OpenPoly experimental Tg with a fixed standardized-Ridge base learner they hold >=90%% coverage with a finite-sample >=1-2alpha guarantee, tie split-conformal at the full pool (n=265), and are up to 25.8%% tighter than split-conformal at intermediate n by removing its single-calibration-split width lottery.
non_circularity: Base learner, seed, train pool and disjoint test set are identical across all three conformal wrappers, so any width/coverage difference is attributable to the wrapper, not the base model or data. Target labels are experimental Tg from OpenPoly literature.

prior_signed_split_conformal_receipt.note: Prior receipt used the Push-20 Van Krevelen ridge as an EXTERNAL base predictor and a 50/50 calibration split; this study re-derives split-conformal with a fixed in-pipeline Ridge so the three wrappers are directly comparable.

purpose: Add a new published conformal baseline (jackknife+/CV+) to the tolerance-robustness uncertainty-quantification battery and test whether its use of the full training pool (no held-out calibration split) yields tighter intervals at matched coverage.

summary.interpretation: All three wrappers hold >=90%% coverage across the grid. Split-conformal's single 50/50 calibration split makes its interval WIDTH high-variance across sample size (it over-covers with a ~430 K width at n=96 when the lone calibration quantile draws high), whereas jackknife+/CV+ average over all leave-one-out fits and produce more stable widths at matched coverage. Jackknife+ is up to 25.8%% TIGHTER than split-conformal at intermediate n (96-192) and ties at the full pool (n=265). The finding is that jackknife+/CV+ remove split-conformal's single-split calibration lottery while retaining a finite-sample >=1-2alpha guarantee -- the relevant robustness property for the small, single-split-fragile datasets typical of coating formulation work.
